findings.title: Six of seven pages open in daylight; this is a night store
findings.evidence: home-m-js-full.png opens on a lit garden path at dusk; pdp-path-m-js-full.png opens on lit fixtures at night and carries the band "בלילה, על השביל". Against that: page-why opens on a green parkland at sunrise (caption "אור נמוך בין עצים"), page-about on a sunlit Jerusalem yard ("בצל") and later a midday tropical garden, page-faq on a grey winter park, page-processing on wet stone steps in flat grey daylight ("גינה ים-תיכונית בקיו"), page-shipping on green olive farmland under a blue sky ("יום מעונן"), page-contact on hard noon sun and orange gravel ("בצהריים"). Only page-guide's two photographs are at dusk. verify.json photo captions confirm: 8 of the 10 photographs are daytime. At 1366 these are full-bleed bands 0-1365 (page-contact-d-js-full.png y=60-365 is a solid orange field), so the first thing every page does is switch the lights on.
findings.fix: Re-shoot the set at the same hour as the home hero — after sundown, fixture lit. Keep only the two dusk frames already in hand (guide). For the four pages where no night frame exists (faq, processing, shipping, contact), drop the photograph entirely rather than substitute daylight: those pages are answers, not places.

vote.why:
The headline count is wrong, three of the named frames are misdescribed, and the fix re-opens a recorded ruling.

**1. The FAQ band is dusk, not "a grey winter park."** verify.json `page-faq-m-js.pageCopy.photos[0]` reads kicker «מקום», caption **«שביל בגינה, בין ערביים»** — a garden path *at dusk*, `captionFound: true`. I cropped page-faq-m-js-full.png y=0-420 and looked: deep blue sky, black tree masses, no sun. It is the darkest crop in the set by the build's own measurement — /home/user/ElmsNest/theme/sections/elmsnest-s-page.liquid lines 13-21 record the measured ratios against the ink in the h1 zone (`guide 1.47 / 2.03 · why 4.15 / 4.17 · FAQ 6.96 / 6.66`) and note that **only** the FAQ crop clears 4.5:1 at both widths, which is why the FAQ is the one page whose h1 sits *on* its band. A 6.96:1 crop against #f4eee3 is not daylight. The critique put its darkest frame in the daylight column.

**2. "8 of the 10 photographs are daytime" is not what verify.json says.** I pulled all ten deployed captions. Explicitly daytime: 3 — why-mechanism «באור יום», shipping «יום מעונן», contact «בצהריים». Explicitly dusk: 3 — guide band «שמיים בין ערביים», guide places «חצר אחת בשעת בין ערביים», faq «שביל בגינה, בין ערביים». Low light / shade: 2 — why band «אור נמוך בין עצים», about band «חצר בירושלים, בצל». Unstated hour: 2 — about inline «ספסל בגינה», processing «גינה ים-תיכונית בקיו». The critique also cites «אור נמוך בין עצים» ("low light between trees") as its evidence that why-solar opens *in daylight*; the caption says the opposite, and the frame is a low golden-hour sun through dark trees, the same register as the home hero.

**3. "page-contact-d-js-full.png y=60-365 is a solid orange field" is a misread of the render.** I sampled the desktop band row by row: the header ends at y≈68 and the band runs to y≈368 (**300 px — exactly the R3 cap at ≥901, not over it**). Row means run (110,86,64) → (182,132,104), a mid-dark terracotta, never a flat field. The crop itself is stone steps on the left third, a near-black clipped shrub filling the centre, gravel only on the right — which is precisely what SPEC §3 specifies for this slot: "(crop on gravel and palm)".

**4. The folds are night, measured.** At 390×844 with JS on, every band is within R3 (guide 167, shipping 197, faq 209, about 213, why/processing/contact 220 px) and occupies 20-26% of the fold; the other ~75% is night ground. Mean fold luminance (Rec.709, 0-255): faq 37.0, about 39.2, why 41.1, shipping 42.3, guide 43.2, processing 48.3, contact 49.7. The home hero the critique holds up as the standard — simplify/verify-after/home-m-js-full.png — measures **47.0** on the same metric. Five of the seven content pages open *darker* than the home page; the two brightest (processing 48.3, contact 49.7) are within 3 points of it. "The first thing every page does is switch the lights on" does not survive the measurement.

**5. The fix re-opens a recorded ruling and asks for something this round cannot buy.** SPEC §1 **R8** rules verbatim: "Every page gets a photograph, **including the two policy pages** — one quiet band each, captioned as a place, no claim — so the seven pages open alike," on the owner's "one family" and the engineer's objection to quiet ("FAQ and processing get no photograph at all… under-delivers the owner's request"). The proposed fix ("drop the photograph entirely… those pages are answers, not places") is R8 reversed, with no showing that R8's reasoning is factually wrong. "Re-shoot the set after sundown" is outside the contract too: SPEC §3 sources all ten from the licensed CC pool in `../pdp3/images/`, and SPEC §6 owner item 2 already records this exact shortage — "every Israeli frame in the pool is midday; the golden-hour places are Mediterranean-looking but photographed elsewhere. One own photograph replaces any band in a picker" — with the rollback wired: every slot in elmsnest-s-page.liquid takes an `image_picker` (`img_contact_band`, `img_proc_band`, …) that overrides the asset without a code change. The round already did what it could about brightness: the section comment records that five photographs (about band, about court, contact, processing, shipping) were **replaced or re-cropped on 2026-09-08**, and that their h1s stay under the band on the night ground.

**What is true.** About's second, inline frame (page-about-m-js-full.png y=1449-1683, caption «ספסל בגינה») is a bright tropical garden genuinely out of key with the set. But it is an inline frame on the second screen, not an opening, so it cannot support "six of seven pages open in daylight"; and R7's rule for loud daylight frames is that they "never sit in a band; where they are used at all they are inline and cropped" — which is exactly where this one is. At most that is a minor, recroppable nit, not a blocker.
vote.scope: Mostly out of scope and factually refuted. The finding's proposed fix directly re-opens SPEC §1 R8 (every page including the policy pages gets a photograph) without showing R8's reasoning to be wrong, and asks for a night shoot that SPEC §3 (fixed licensed pool) and §6 owner item 2 (no Israeli dusk frame exists; picker is the rollback) already record as unavailable this round. The one in-scope residue — About's bright inline tropical garden at y=1449 — is R7-compliant (inline, not a band) and is a minor re-crop, not a blocker.

What I measured:

The mirror /home/user/ElmsNest/brief/side-pages/pages/verify/mirrors/page-contact/index.html does carry required="required" on contact[name], contact[email], contact[phone] and contact[body], with labels "שם מלא", "כתובת מייל", "מספר טלפון", "הודעה (נדרשת)". I cropped page-contact-m-js-full.png (390x2494, the 30-72% band) and the render matches: only the message label carries "(נדרשת)". So the description of the pixels is accurate.
2. But the identical block already exists in the PRE-round mirror /home/user/ElmsNest/brief/inventory/page-contact/index.html — same label strings, same four required attributes, same Kalles block id (…__contact_form_4UVE84) and the same second copy inside the ContactFormAsk modal. This round changed nothing about the form; the "one marked, four required" mismatch is the merchant's existing stock state, not a regression this round introduced.
3. The markup is not in this repo. `find /home/user/ElmsNest/theme -name '*contact*'` returns only assets/ens-page-contact-band.jpg, templates/page.contact-us.json and snippets/elmsnest-s-contact.liquid (an unrelated "send a photo" line). 4. It is a recorded ruling. SPEC.md §2 (line 41-42): «templates/page.contact-us.json — ["ens_page", "contact_form"], the stock Kalles contact form untouched (P1)». P1 (../simplify/SPEC.md §2) is «Every ACTION uses the pattern a Shopify shopper already knows»; the same ruling is repeated in brief/side-pages/pages/BRIEF.md:64 and in all five concept NOTES. The section's contact branch (elmsnest-s-page.liquid, `when 'contact'`, lines 570-586) only prints the band photo, the h1, an optional lead and an optional email line — it emits no form field. The critique does not show that P1's reasoning is factually wrong; it simply asks to edit the untouched form.

Legitimate residue: the mismatch is real and worth an owner item (the fix lives in Shopify admin / the vendor theme's locale, not in this repo). That is a note, not a blocker against this round's build.
vote.scope: Out of this round's contract: the contact form is stock Kalles markup, explicitly ruled untouched (SPEC §2 / P1), absent from the repo's theme files, and identical in the pre-round inventory mirror — so nothing this round built causes or can fix it. findings.title: The blue solar-cell macro reads as this store's panel
findings.evidence: page-why-m-js-full.png y≈860-1160: an extreme close-up of a polycrystalline PV module filling the frame, electric blue, kicker "מנגנון", caption "תא סולארי מקרוב, באור יום", credit Guilhem Vellut. It sits immediately under the "איך זה עובד בפועל" 1-2-3 explanation, so it presents as the panel on the goods — at a scale (utility module, cell busbars) no garden lamp has. It is also the only cold-blue frame anywhere in the store, against the navy-and-gold of home and PDP.
findings.fix: Remove it. If the mechanism needs a picture, shoot the actual panel on one of the 27 products you stock, at that product's size, and caption it with the product name — otherwise let the three numbered steps carry the explanation alone.

vote.why:
Measured the exact frame and two of the finding's three load-bearing assertions fail.

WHAT IS TRUE. Row-scan of /home/user/ElmsNest/brief/side-pages/pages/verify/page-why-m-js-full.png puts the photo at y=905–1138 (310x233 inline frame, not a band), caption at y≈1160–1185. It is the Wikimedia "Close-up of a polycrystalline solar PV panel" (brief/side-pages/pages/IMAGES.md line 6, asset theme/assets/ens-page-why-cell.jpg, 1200x800, 192 KB), kicker מנגנון, caption "תא סולארי מקרוב, באור יום", credit Guilhem Vellut. It does sit under "איך זה עובד בפועל" (elmsnest-s-page.liquid:260, photo rendered at :270-274). verify.json page-why-m-js confirms kickerFound/captionFound/creditFound all true, kickerMarks 2.

FAILURE 1 — "the only cold-blue frame anywhere in the store" is false. I scanned all seven page shots plus home-m-js-full.png and pdp-path-m-js-full.png for row-average hue 175-265 with sat>0.20. The shipping band (מטע זיתים, יום מעונן, Dimitry B) measures RGB (71,105,146) / (69,102,142) at y=100-130 — hue 213, sat 0.51, i.e. the SAME hue as the cell frame and MORE saturated than the cell frame's page-render average (hue 212, sat 0.43). I cropped it: cool blue-grey mountains and a cold overcast sky across the full band. FAQ y=60-70 is hue 207 as well. Further, the site's own night ground measures RGB (9,16,29) = hue ~219; the cell frame is hue 212 — 7 degrees from the store's own navy. It is the navy hue at higher value, not a foreign cold cast "against the navy-and-gold".

FAILURE 2 — "at a scale (utility module, cell busbars) no garden lamp has" is not supported by the pixels. I opened the 1200x800 asset: the frame contains no scale reference at all — no module edge, no frame rail, no surroundings, no hand, no horizon. Polycrystalline cells with silver fingers and busbars are exactly the cell type used on small garden solar lamps; nothing in the frame distinguishes a 300 W module from a 2 W lamp panel. The caption itself says "מקרוב" — it declares that it is a macro before it says anything else.

FAILURE 3 — "presents as the panel on the goods" is contradicted by the page's own grammar. SPEC §1 R5 exists precisely for this: every caption opens with a kicker naming the KIND of picture. The four place frames say מקום; this one says מנגנון. The copy it illustrates is category-generic — h1 "למה תאורה סולארית — ומתי לא", step 1 "הפאנל הסולארי נטען מאור היום" (definite-generic, no possessive). I grepped the section for שלנו: one hit, on the About trio (line 358), nowhere near this photo. No product name, no possessive, alt is deliberately blank so the caption carries the meaning (snippet contract, elmsnest-s-page-photo.liquid header). SPEC §3's honesty constraint is "No frame shows a lamp that could read as a store product" — this frame has no lamp. BRIEF §3's non-negotiables (no fabricated claims) are not touched.

SCOPE. SPEC §3 commissions this exact photograph for this exact slot with this exact kicker and caption, and R5 records the honesty judge's reasoning for the kicker device (8, "all nine say what they are before they say anything else"). "Remove it" re-opens that recorded ruling, and the finding never engages the kicker except to quote it — it does not show the ruling's reasoning is factually wrong.

RESIDUAL (not the finding as filed, and not a blocker): on page-why-d-js-full.png the inline frame runs ~1230 px wide and ~830 px tall (y≈935–1765), which is wider than R9's 62-68 ch reading measure and is the loudest object on the desktop page. If anything survives here it is a desktop-width/measure note against R9, not a misrepresentation blocker, and its fix is a narrower frame, not deletion.
vote.scope: out-of-scope (re-opens SPEC §1 R5 / §3's commissioned מנגנון frame) and evidence-wrong: the "only cold-blue frame" claim and the "utility-module scale" claim both fail measurement

vote.why:
The observation is mostly accurate but the diagnosis ("blocker", "page-processing should not exist") is wrong, and the repetition it names is contractually mandated, inherited, and reciprocal — not a defect.

WHAT I MEASURED

findings.title: Every photograph is kickered "מקום"
findings.evidence: verify.json photos across all seven pages: 9 of 10 kickers are the single word "מקום" (the tenth is "מנגנון" on the PV macro). The kicker adds nothing the caption does not already say — "מקום · חצר בירושלים, בצל", "מקום · מטע זיתים, יום מעונן".
findings.fix: Drop the kicker span. Keep caption and credit on one line: "חצר בירושלים, בצל · צילום: RonAlmog (CC BY 2.0)".

vote.why:
The counts are right and the render is right — and neither supports the fix.

MEASURED. verify.json (all 42 page/breakpoint/JS entries agree): ten photographs, kickers = מקום ×9, מנגנון ×1 (why-solar's PV macro), every kickerFound/captionFound/creditFound true. The two quoted lines are verbatim (about band "מקום · חצר בירושלים, בצל", shipping band "מקום · מטע זיתים, יום מעונן"). Crops of page-shipping-m-js-fold.png (0–420), page-about-m-js-full.png (0–500) and page-why-m-js-full.png (1150–1500) show the real thing: a 12.5 px serif gold word, a muted middot, then the caption on the SAME line (theme/sections/elmsnest-s-page.liquid:628–631: .ens-page__kick 12.5px/var(--env2-gold), .ens-page__dot margin-inline 7px, .ens-page__cap 13px/ink-2, .ens-page__credit 12.5px/mute on its own line). The kicker costs zero lines and zero height; all seven pages are already far under budget (2.63–4.05 screens vs targets 4–6).

WHY IT FAILS.
1) It re-opens a recorded ruling. SPEC §1 R5: "Caption grammar = field. Every caption opens with a kicker naming the kind of picture — «מקום» or «מנגנון» — then the subject and the hour, then the credit on its own line", carried by the honesty guardian's 8 ("all nine say what they are before they say anything else"). The finding asks to delete precisely R5 and does not show R5's reasoning is factually wrong — it asserts redundancy, which is the thing R5 already weighed.
2) The redundancy claim misreads the captions. Several do not say "place" at all: "שמיים בין ערביים" is a sky; "אור נמוך בין עצים" ("low light among trees"), sitting on the why-solar page, reads as a demonstration of our lamp's output unless the kicker declares it a licensed picture of a place. That is the honesty rule of BRIEF §3 and SPEC §3 ("No frame shows a lamp that could read as a store product; the two frames that contain a fixture… are captioned as places"), and R8 ("captioned as a place, no claim") for the two policy pages, where an olive grove above משלוחים והחזרות has no other explanation.
3) The 9:1 split is the argument for the label, not against it. My why-page crop shows both terms in the same slot on one page — "מקום · אור נמוך בין עצים" and, one screen down, "מנגנון · תא סולארי מקרוב, באור יום". The contrast that makes מנגנון legible exists only because the other frames say מקום; keeping the odd one and dropping the class destroys the distinction rather than tightening it.
4) The kicker is structural, not editorial. It is hardcoded at the ten call sites (elmsnest-s-page.liquid:161,175,251,271,331,365,396,471,510,574) while caption and credit are schema settings and the image is an owner picker. It is the invariant that survives an owner swapping a band photo and rewriting its caption — remove it and an owner-edited caption can turn a place picture into a claim.
5) The proposed replacement breaks a second half of R5 and the family. It merges the credit onto the caption line ("…, בצל · צילום: RonAlmog (CC BY 2.0)"), whereas R5 and the render put the credit on its own muted line; and the PDP the pages must join already opens with a kicker line (snippets/elmsnest-s-pdp-kicker.liquid, SIMPLIFY SPEC §86, PDP2 BRIEF §16/26), which is exactly the "same shop" grammar R2 was ruled for.

Residual: one could still argue the gold weight makes the kicker slightly louder than a taxonomy mark needs to be — but that is a tone note about .ens-page__kick's color, not the "drop the span" fix filed, and the finding offers no measurement against it.
vote.scope: SPEC §1 R5 (caption grammar) with §3/§8 and BRIEF §3 honesty; the kicker span in /home/user/ElmsNest/theme/snippets/elmsnest-s-page-photo.liquid, its ten call sites and .ens-page__kick/.ens-page__dot CSS in /home/user/ElmsNest/theme/sections/elmsnest-s-page.liquid, measured against /home/user/ElmsNest/brief/side-pages/pages/verify/verify.json and the shipping/about/why mobile shots.

findings.title: Two captions describe something the frame does not show
findings.evidence: page-faq-d-js-full.png: caption "שביל בגינה, בין ערביים" over a wide asphalt avenue through a memorial park — leafless winter trees, a monument on a plinth centre-frame, pale overcast sky. (1) FAQ caption "שביל בגינה, בין ערביים" (a path in a garden, at twilight). I opened the deployed band — /home/user/ElmsNest/brief/side-pages/pages/verify/page-faq-d-js-full.png cropped 0,0,1366,900 — and the source asset /home/user/ElmsNest/theme/assets/ens-page-faq-band.jpg (1200×1176). IMAGES.md and SPEC §3 name the source: Wikimedia `wm_a17b65ac2a`, "View toward Perennial Garden NBG" — Norfolk Botanical Garden. It is a garden, not "a memorial park"; the centre object is a garden fountain in a perennial parterre, not "a monument on a plinth".
Sky, measured on the source (RGB samples): top of sky (300,30)=(100,132,173) and (520,40)=(144,178,224) — strongly blue, B−R ≈ +73 to +80; descending through (640,320)=(201,223,247), (640,440)=(230,235,239) to the horizon band (640,500)=(206,202,190) and (720,505)=(241,240,236) — warm, R ≥ B. A blue-overhead → warm-horizon gradient on a clear sky is twilight/golden hour; a "pale overcast sky" is flat grey top to bottom with no blue and no warm band. The claim "neither a garden path nor dusk" is refuted on both nouns and the hour. "שביל" claims only a path; it does not claim a surface, so "wide asphalt avenue" is not a caption error.

(2) The guide. verify.json (page-guide-m-js.pageCopy.photos) shows exactly two photos, captions "שמיים בין ערביים" and "חצר אחת בשעת בין ערביים" — and the critic concedes the first is honest, so nothing there is a caption fault. findings.title: Contact: three of four fields are silently required, and the phone pattern rejects real Israeli numbers
findings.evidence: mirrors/page-contact/index.html — every control carries required="required": contact[name], contact[email], contact[phone] and contact[body]. Only the message is labelled as required: page-contact-m-js-full.png shows labels שם מלא / כתובת מייל / מספר טלפון with no marker and only הודעה (נדרשת) at y≈780. The phone input also carries pattern="[0-9\-]*", so +972 50 123 4567 (or any number typed with spaces or a +) is rejected with the browser's generic "match the requested format". A first-time visitor who does not want to hand over a phone number, or who types the country code, simply cannot send the message — and nothing on the page told them phone was mandatory.
findings.fix: In theme/templates/page.contact-us.json, replace the vendor contact-form block with a form whose only required fields are contact[email] and contact[body]; drop required and pattern from contact[phone] and label it מספר טלפון (לא חובה). Mark the two genuinely required labels the same way the message is marked. Add autocomplete="name|email|tel" to the three inputs so mobile autofill works.

vote.why:
The markup facts check out, but the finding re-opens a ruling this round recorded with these exact facts already on the table, and its proposed fix is not performable in the file it names.

What I measured. In /home/user/ElmsNest/brief/side-pages/pages/verify/mirrors/page-contact/index.html the visible form is `<form ... id="AaWVmZjg2Nll3aXplT__contact_form_4UVE84" class="contact-form">` at byte 167459. Its four controls are: `required="required" type="text" name="contact[name]"`, `required="required" type="email" name="contact[email]" ... aria-required="true" required="required"`, `required="required" type="tel" name="contact[phone]" pattern="[0-9\-]*"`, `<textarea name="contact[body]" required="required">`. Labels are שם מלא / כתובת מייל / מספר טלפון / הודעה (נדרשת). I cropped page-contact-m-js-full.png (390x2494) at y 520-1120 and read it: only הודעה carries "(נדרשת)"; email and phone carry no marker. So the four-required claim, the label claim and the pattern are all literally true, and `+972 50 123 4567` would indeed fail `[0-9\-]*`. (The second occurrence of these names at byte ~219275 is the global `ContactFormAsk` modal, not this page's form.)

Why it is still refuted.

1. Out of scope — an informed, recorded ruling. SPEC.md §2 states the contract for this exact file: "`templates/page.contact-us.json` — `["ens_page", "contact_form"]`, the stock Kalles contact form untouched (P1)". The same ruling is repeated in the round brief (pages/BRIEF.md line 64, "the form is stock, P1") and in all five concept notes (atlas, band, field, letter, quiet NOTES.md). P1 is simplify/SPEC.md §2: every ACTION uses the pattern a Shopify shopper already knows.

2. The ruling's reasoning is not factually wrong, because the required phone was already on the record when it was made. The pre-round inventory audit /home/user/ElmsNest/brief/inventory/AUDIT-content-pages.md line 197 records verbatim: "all four fields `required` (phone `pattern="[0-9\-]*"`)"; line 264: "phone is `required` with `[0-9\-]*`"; line 258 names the consequence ("every 'send a photo' link lands on a contact form that cannot take a photo and requires a phone number"). The lead ruled to keep the stock form knowing this. The finding brings no new fact against that reasoning.

3. The round did not introduce it. `git show` of the previous revision of theme/templates/page.contact-us.json shows the identical `contact-form` section with the same `_contact_col` / `_contact-form` blocks (contact_col_39rTtM, contact_form_4UVE84). This round only added `ens_page` above it. The defect is pre-existing vendor behaviour.

4. The proposed fix is not possible where it is aimed. page.contact-us.json is a Shopify JSON template: it can only name section types and their schema settings — it cannot carry form markup, `required`, `pattern` or `autocomplete` attributes. The `_contact-form` block exposes exactly one setting, `success_message`. And `sections/contact-form.liquid` is not in this repo at all (`ls /home/user/ElmsNest/theme/sections/` has no contact-form.liquid; the audit line 214 calls it a Kalles file kept "as a schema reference"), so honouring the fix means forking a vendor section — the opposite of the P1 ruling. The labels (שם מלא, הודעה (נדרשת)) come from the live theme's Hebrew locale, not from any file in /home/user/ElmsNest/theme/locales (no such directory) — i.e. Shopify admin work, not this round's surface.

5. Two overstatements. "Rejects real Israeli numbers" — the domestic formats 0501234567 and 050-1234567 both match `[0-9\-]*`; only the +972/spaced form is rejected. "Simply cannot send the message" — the page's own right column prints "דוא״ל: info@elmsnest.com" as an explicit alternative channel (the `_liquid` block in page.contact-us.json), so the visitor is not cut off.

Honest residue: the mislabelled required phone is a genuine friction and belongs where SPEC §6 keeps such things — an owner/admin item (locale text plus a vendor-form decision for a later round), not a blocker against this build.
vote.scope: Out of this round's contract: SPEC.md §2 (and pages/BRIEF.md §3, all five concept NOTES) rule the stock Kalles contact form untouched under P1, with the four-required/`[0-9\-]*` phone already recorded in the pre-round inventory (AUDIT-content-pages.md 197/264). Belongs as an owner item alongside SPEC §6 — Shopify locale text plus a vendor-section decision — not a blocker on elmsnest-s-page.liquid / page.contact-us.json.

findings.title: Nine of eleven photographs carry the identical "מקום" kicker, one of them from Kew Gardens

vote.why:
Measured all three parts of the claim; the count is wrong, the Kew reading misreads the render, and the kicker constancy is a recorded ruling.

1) COUNT. There are ten photographs, not eleven. /home/user/ElmsNest/brief/side-pages/pages/SPEC.md §3 is titled "The photographs (ten, ≤ 3 per page)"; /home/user/ElmsNest/brief/side-pages/pages/IMAGES.md has exactly 10 asset rows; `grep -n "kicker:" /home/user/ElmsNest/theme/sections/elmsnest-s-page.liquid` returns exactly 10 literals (lines 161, 175, 251, 271, 331, 365, 396, 471, 510, 574) — nine 'מקום', one 'מנגנון'. verify.json pageCopy.photos over the seven -m-js keys yields the same 10 (guide 2, why 2, about 2, faq/processing/shipping/contact 1 each). The visitor's own enumeration sums to 10 while the title says 11, so it is 9 of 10.

2) THE KICKER IS A RECORDED RULING WITH A STATED FUNCTION. SPEC §1 R5: "Caption grammar = field. Every caption opens with a kicker naming the kind of picture — «מקום» or «מנגנון» — then the subject and the hour, then the credit on its own line", carried by the honesty judge's 8 and the quote "all nine say what they are before they say anything else". /home/user/ElmsNest/brief/side-pages/pages/concepts/field/IMAGES.md line 3 states the purpose outright: the kicker names what the picture is — a place or a mechanism — "so no photograph can be read as the store's product". It is a closed two-word set by design; constancy is the mechanism, not an oversight. The proposed replacements make it worse on the ruling's own terms: «שביל» and «חצר» are the store's own place/category words (the guide's four labels are שביל · קיר · גינה · מרפסת, R4), so a kicker «שביל» over a photograph re-couples the frame to a sellable category — exactly what R5 exists to prevent. I cropped /home/user/ElmsNest/brief/side-pages/pages/verify/page-guide-m-js-full.png (0,0,390,500) and page-processing-m-js-full.png (0,150,390,360): the kicker is an ~11–12 px muted/gold run-in word at the head of a one-line figcaption, followed by a middot and the subject, with the credit on the line below — credit-grade micro type, the register in which a repeated prefix reads as grammar (like "Photo:"), not as repetition of a heading.

3) THE KEW READING IS WRONG. In page-processing-m-js-full.png at y≈265–350 the caption reads «מקום · גינה ים-תיכונית בקיו» with «צילום: Swphotouk (CC BY 4.0)» underneath — the caption names Kew and credits the photographer under licence. The build is in fact stricter than the contract: SPEC §3 specified the vaguer caption «גינה ים-תיכונית, אחר הצהריים», and the deployed copy added «בקיו». By contrast the About inline frame is Singapore Botanic Gardens (wm_faf95922bd, IMAGES.md) captioned only «ספסל בגינה» — so the Kew band is the most disclosed foreign frame in the set, not the dishonest one. BRIEF.md §3's rule is "unverified information is never presented as fact"; a located, credited, licensed public-garden photograph presents nothing as fact that is not.

SPEC §3 assigns wm_51c75f4f98 to the processing band, cropped 0,1400,3840,1160 → 1600×483 (IMAGES.md) — a paving/planting strip with sky and temple out of frame (SHORTLIST row 20: "no temple in frame so no landmark"), so R7's ban on noon panoramas owning a fold is respected. One own photograph replaces any band in a picker" — and R7 bars the Haifa terraces, desert cactus and bougainvillea noon frames from bands, so "swap in one of the Israeli images already in the set" has no legal candidate this round. findings.title: __spine carries five of the seven pages; the family reads as one ruled list

WHAT I MEASURED
1. Device census (grep on theme/sections/elmsnest-s-page.liquid): __spine does appear once each on guide (l.206), why (l.261), about (l.346), processing (l.489) and shipping (l.539) — 5 of 7. 3. Crop of page-guide-m-js-full.png y1300–1680: the guide's spine is lettered א/ב/ג, not numbered. That is R1 verbatim — "a lettered spine for the purposes". The finding cites the guide's spine as evidence against the ruling that mandates it.

THE DUPLICATION CLAIM IS MISREAD AND OUT OF CONTRACT
4. "shipping's __pair + __spine also publish the identical three numbers" is false on the __pair. Crop of page-shipping-m-js-full.png y600–1060 and liquid l.526–535: shipping's __pair is the COSTS list — חינם / 29.90 ₪ — and carries no timing number at all. The three timings on shipping live only in the __spine, and each row there carries its own explanatory sentence (warehouses outside Israel, split parcels, the business-day definition); processing's __plate is a bare three-cell label/value figure. Same facts, two devices, different content — not "the identical table twice".
5. The repetition is recorded copy, not a build slip. COPY-SOURCE.md l.346–348 (processing plate) and l.403–407 (shipping spine) both carry 1–3 / 7–14 / 8–17 in the source, and its consumer-term census l.558–561 lists each number as required on processing AND shipping AND the FAQ. SPEC §4 says everything not on its five-item list stays byte-identical to COPY-SOURCE; BRIEF §3 makes those delivery terms a non-negotiable that may be compacted but "not removed". "Delete the duplicated timing table from one of processing/shipping" would strip a consumer-protection term from the shipping page — the page a customer opens to find it — and is a copy change §4 does not authorise. The build already does the honest version of the fix: processing's lead (schema l.827) reads «המספרים כאן זהים למדיניות המשלוחים המלאה — אין הבטחות נפרדות», shipping's note says «המספרים כאן זהים למדיניות המשלוחים המלאה», and shipping already cross-links to processing (ens_proc) while both link the binding policy.
6. The proposed fix does not reach its own cap and partly describes what is already there. Shipping's cancellation block is already __trio, not a list; giving shipping the __plate would make it MORE like processing, not less; and none of the three moves removes shipping's __spine, so the spine would still stand on four or five pages.

SCOPE
"Cap __spine at two pages" is a rule that exists nowhere in the contract. SPEC §1 R1 rules the opposite principle — "Devices vary with the content" — and the designer judge's own sentence quoted there ("no page reads as one ruled list repeated four times") is a per-page test the build passes: the spine is used exactly where the content is an ordered sequence (the four purposes, day→evening→meaning, the three principles, the order's three stages, the three timing stages) and another device is used wherever it is not (costs → pair, cancellation → trio, figures → plate, places → frame, questions → accordion, contact → none). Re-opening R1 needs a demonstration that R1's reasoning is factually wrong; the finding offers a count, and the count is consistent with R1.

findings.title: The photo credit is announced before the page title
findings.evidence: Source order in elmsnest-s-page.liquid is photo → figcaption → head, so on six of seven pages (all but faq) the reader meets צילום: … before the h1. page-contact-m-js-full.png y=308–322 reads צילום: Josh Evnin from Chicago, IL, USA (CC BY-SA 2.0) — raw Flickr uploader metadata with a US city, at 12.5px — and the h1 יצירת קשר only appears at y=365. vote.why:
The geometry in the evidence is real, but it does not describe a defect, and both halves of the proposed fix are wrong.

WHAT I MEASURED
• Source order: `snippets/elmsnest-s-page-photo.liquid` L159–188 — `<figure>` = `div.ens-page__box` (img) then `<figcaption>`; the section prints `div.ens-page__head` (h1 + lead) after the figure on guide/why/about/proc/ship/contact, and inside the band only on FAQ (h1_on). So "six of seven" is correct as a DOM fact.
• Crop of `verify/page-contact-m-js-full.png` y=240–470: band ends y≈288; caption «מקום · גן בחיפה, בצהריים» ≈y300; credit «צילום: Josh Evnin from Chicago, IL, USA (CC BY-SA 2.0)» ≈y316; h1 «יצירת קשר» ≈y365. Coordinates check out.
• But the crop also shows the hierarchy the finding omits: h1 is 32px serif near-white (`--env2-ink`, 44px at ≥901), caption 13px `--env2-ink-2`, credit 12.5px `--env2-mute` (CSS at elmsnest-s-page.liquid L~625–631). Nothing is pushed off the fold: `page-contact-m-js-fold.png` and `page-guide-m-js-fold.png` (390×844) both show band + caption + h1 + lead + the first section heading inside the first screen — R3's ≤220px band cap doing exactly its job. No reader "meets the credit before the title" in any perceptual sense; a 12.5px muted licence line under a photo is not an announcement.
• Desktop: crop of `page-contact-d-js-full.png` x466–1366, y370–540 — credit y≈413, h1 y≈478, as claimed. But the credit already spans absolute x≈1001–1301, i.e. exactly the 300px inline-start rail (`.ens-page__figcap-in{grid-template-columns:minmax(0,300px) minmax(0,68ch)}` with `.ens-page__cap,.ens-page__credit{grid-column:1}`, L~740). The fix's own desktop remedy — "into the empty 300px rail that figcap-in already grids for" — is already shipped; the caption is in the margin per R9, not in the reading measure.

WHY THE FIX IS WORSE
• "Print ens-page__head immediately after the band's __box" puts every content page's h1 *inside* a `<figure>` — the page title becomes part of a figure's content on six pages. The alternative reading, lifting the figcaption out of the figure, is invalid (figcaption must be a child of figure) and would orphan the licence from the image.
• Every band's alt is empty by design (schema L769: «ריק = תמונה דקורטיבית; הכיתוב נושא את המשמעות», and no alt_* setting carries a default → all ten render `alt=""`). The figcaption is therefore the picture's only accessible meaning; moving it below the lead detaches a decorative image from the text that describes it — a genuine a11y regression traded for a DOM-order preference.
• "Strip the uploader's home town" contradicts the record: `IMAGES.md` row for `ens-page-contact-band.jpg` gives the Commons author field verbatim as "Josh Evnin from Chicago, IL, USA" and the credit line as printed; the section default (L851) matches it byte for byte. BRIEF §3 forbids presenting anything but the verified record; rewriting an attribution string away from the source page is the wrong direction for this project's honesty rules.

FAMILY / RULINGS
• The family does the same thing: `pdp2/verify-after/pdp-path-m-js-full.png` puts the muted kicker line («תאורת שביל, עמוד וגינה · מתאים כדי לראות את הדרך») between the opening gallery and the h1. The home band (`elmsnest-s-home-band.liquid`) owes no credit — it is store-owned — so it offers no counter-example.
• R5 is a recorded ruling adopting field's caption grammar precisely because "all nine say what they are before they say anything else"; the picture declaring itself with its licence, at the picture, is the ruled grammar. The finding asserts a preference against it without showing the ruling's reasoning to be factually wrong. R2's "directly under it" distinguishes on-band from under-band h1s, not the presence of the figure's own caption.

Residual: the contact credit is the longest of the ten and does fill a full 390px line, so a shorter author string would look tidier — but that is taste against a recorded attribution, not a "should" defect.

vote.why:
The arithmetic is right but the reading of it is wrong, and two of its four "widths" collapse on measurement.

WHAT I CONFIRMED. `elmsnest-v2-core.liquid:21` sets `--env2-w:1240px`, `--env2-gut:clamp(20px,4vw,64px)`; at 1366 the wrap is 63..1303. `elmsnest-s-page.liquid:736` is as quoted. Cropping the PNGs and thresholding each row against its own median, the measure column runs 330..938 (608px ≈ 68ch) and the heading track ends at 1302, so ~268px at 63..333 carries nothing on guide/faq/shipping below the band. So far the finding is accurate.

WHY IT STILL FAILS. (1) "Four different content widths" counts ragged inline-END edges and ignores that every in-scope block is flush to ONE inline-start spine. Measured right edges on the real shots: band caption 1302, credit 1302, lead 1302, h1 1301, h2 1302, processing's three-cell plate 1302, about's inline photo 1302, guide's places frame 1303 (CSS `.ens-page__sec > .ens-page__frame{grid-column:1/-1}` = the grid's own width, not a new one). In an RTL page that single 1302/1303 edge is the edge a reader tracks; the inline-end rags because the devices differ in weight. That is a flush-inline-start composition, not four arbitrary containers.

(2) "On every page" is false. The contact branch (elmsnest-s-page.liquid:573-585) emits only a band plus `env2-wrap ens-page__head` — there is no `.ens-page__sec` grid on that page at all, so the 269px gap it describes does not exist there. The 98..1268 panel it cites as evidence I measured exactly (98..1267, 1170px, panel bg rgb(15,26,47) at y=900): that is the stock Kalles `contact-form` section in `templates/page.contact-us.json` (`section_layout:"container"`, `scheme-env2-night`), which SPEC §2 rules "the stock Kalles contact form untouched (P1)". It is out of this round's contract, not a width this build chose. And on processing/about/why the 63..333 strip is not dead: the plate and the inline photos measure 63..1302 there.

(3) The proposed fix would create the misalignment it claims to cure. The h1-on-band and the caption/credit are `env2-wrap` by construction inside `elmsnest-s-page-photo.liquid:170,178` (`.ens-page__onband-in env2-wrap`, `.ens-page__figcap-in env2-wrap`), so they sit at 1303 no matter what. Setting the section wrap to `calc(300px+64px+68ch)` and centring it moves every h2 and body column to ~197..1169 while the h1 and its credit stay at 1302 — one spine becomes two.

(4) Scope. SPEC §1 R9 is a recorded ruling ("Desktop is a designed layout, not a phone column centred in 1366: the reading measure is 62–68 ch on its own column with the captions in the margin where the device has one"), and the CSS comment at line 723 cites it by name. The two-column asymmetric grid with heading and captions in the inline-start margin is that ruling executed. The finding argues from the leftover pixels alone; it does not show R9's reasoning is factually wrong, so it re-opens a ruling it is not entitled to re-open.

Residual truth worth recording, not as a "should": the 268px inline-end rag is real and constant at every width ≥ the wrap, and on guide/faq/shipping nothing but the full-bleed band ever reaches into it. If the owner dislikes the rag, the honest lever is widening the measure track — not centring the grid, which breaks the spine.

findings.title: The FAQ chevron never points down or up

Visible in page-faq-m-js-full.png: the open row at y≈450 shows › and closed rows at y≈580 show ‹ — twelve disclosure rows where nothing signals expandable and open/closed differ only by mirroring.
findings.fix: Line 702 → border-block-end:1px solid var(--env2-gold);border-inline-start:1px solid var(--env2-gold);transform:rotate(45deg) (bottom+right in RTL, which points down); keep line 703's rotate(-135deg) so open points up.

vote.why: Confirmed on all three checks. (1) Code: elmsnest-s-page.liquid:702 is exactly as quoted — border-block-end + border-inline-end + rotate(45deg), open rotate(-135deg); line 153 hardcodes dir="rtl" on the section, so inline-end is the LEFT edge. Bordered corner = bottom-left (-1,+1 y-down); rotate(45deg) clockwise maps it to (-1.41,0) = LEFT, rotate(-135deg) to (+1.41,0) = RIGHT. (2) Render: cropped page-faq-m-js-full.png (390x2242) at y 380-720 and read it at 3x — the <details open> row shows a right-pointing ›, the two closed rows below show left-pointing ‹. No down/up chevron. Twelve details total (4 each in #faq-products, #faq-orders, #faq-policies). (3) Decisive: the theme has already fixed this exact bug twice and left the derivation in comments. elmsnest-s-coll-header.liquid:149-153 — "border-inline-start = the RIGHT edge, so the bordered corner is bottom-right (+1,+1); rotate(45deg) … = DOWN. border-inline-end gave bottom-left (-1,+1) → (-1.41,0) = LEFT, the shape of a back link." elmsnest-s-pdp-facts.liquid:238-243 — "rotate(45deg) → DOWN when closed, rotate(-135deg) → UP when open. The old -45deg / 135deg pair pointed RIGHT / LEFT, i.e. back / forward in RTL," shipping border-inline-start + border-block-end + rotate(45deg). The proposed fix is byte-for-byte that house pattern and keeps SPEC's "logical properties only" rule; the PDP is one of the two family references this round must join. Minor overstatements in the claim, not fatal: "nothing signals expandable" is too strong (an inline-end chevron does read as a disclosure/back-link affordance in RTL), and the y-coordinates are approximate (open mark nearer y≈500, closed y≈655). The substance — the pair is a left/right mirror instead of a down/up rotation, and the open state points backwards — holds.

findings.title: The __pair label column is too narrow and breaks the value off the label
findings.evidence: elmsnest-s-page.liquid:747 — minmax(0,.8fr) minmax(0,1.4fr) gives the dt ~220px of the 607px column. In page-shipping-d-js-full.png (עלויות משלוח, item 1) the label wraps as משלוח לנקודת איסוף בישראל / — חינם, dangling the em dash and the price onto their own line while 269px of the wrap sits empty to the left.

vote.why:
I could not refute it — the render does what the lens says.

MEASURED, page-shipping-d-js-full.png (1366x2146). Adaptive-threshold scan of the hairlines that bound `.ens-page__pair > div` puts all three rules of the עלויות משלוח list at x 333..938 — a 606px row (the lens said 607). With line 747's `minmax(0,.8fr) minmax(0,1.4fr)` and `gap:0 24px`, the dt gets 582*0.8/2.2 = 211.6px and the dd 370.4px (the lens said ~220; close enough).

Item 1's dt does wrap, and it wraps exactly as described. Per-scanline extents inside y 563..632: the first line runs x 726..937 (the dt column, full) and x 552..703 (the dd, "לכל הזמנה, בלי מינימום."); the second line is x 891..939 only — 49px. The strongest thing against refuting: on mobile the same string fits whole. In page-shipping-m-js-full.png the pair rows span x 20..369 (350px single column, line 670's `minmax(0,1fr)`) and «משלוח לנקודת איסוף בישראל — חינם» sits on ONE line. So this is not long copy — it is line 747 handing the label 212px at 1366 where 390 gives it 350px. Copy is not the lever either (SPEC §4 freezes the string byte-for-byte against COPY-SOURCE.md).

Not out of contract: SPEC §1 R1 records the two-column definition list as the device for the power sources, and R9 asks for a designed desktop; neither ruling fixes the .8/1.4 ratio, so this does not re-open a recorded ruling.

TWO CORRECTIONS to the write-up, neither fatal to it:
1. "269px of the wrap sits empty to the left" is wrong. The wrapped line leaves 165px empty inside the dt line box (726..891); the unused space in the dd on line 1 is 219px (dd column 333..703, text 552..703). No measurement yields 269.
2. The PROPOSED FIX is unsafe as written. `.ens-page__pair > div` is a separate grid per row (line 670), not one shared grid, so `auto` sizes each row's label column to that row's own max-content and the rows stop aligning — on the guide (the device's other use, page-guide-d-js-full.png, hairlines y 1999/2127/2206/2285, same 333..938) the three dts have max-contents of roughly 210/250/215px, so three different column edges. vote.scope: theme/sections/elmsnest-s-page.liquid line 747 (desktop .ens-page__pair grid ratio); affects the shipping page's עלויות משלוח item 1 at >=901px only. Mobile (line 670) and the guide §03 pair render correctly.

findings.title: h1_on is a hardcoded page name, not the grammar it documents
findings.evidence: elmsnest-s-page.liquid:107–110 — assign ens_h1_on = false / if ens_key == 'faq'. The snippet header of elmsnest-s-page-photo.liquid documents "true only where the crop was MEASURED >= 4.5:1 against the ink under the h1", but nothing measures anything. FAQ gets the on-band h1 (page-faq-m-js-full.png, שאלות נפוצות over dark asphalt, correctly scrimmed) because it is named in an if; the other six sit off-band because their photographs are too bright.
findings.fix: Make h1_on a per-page schema boolean the owner sets after checking the crop, and once the daylight frames are replaced turn it on for guide, why and about so the band behaves like home's hero.

vote.why:
The finding's factual core — "nothing measures anything" — is false, and I reproduced the measurement it says does not exist.

1) The measurement is recorded, with numbers, in the same file, 94 lines above the line the evidence cites. /home/user/ElmsNest/theme/sections/elmsnest-s-page.liquid:13–22: "Where the h1 sits (R2 — measured, recorded, not assumed). The band crops of assets/ens-page-*.jpg were measured against the ink #f4eee3 in the zone the h1 occupies at the bottom of a 390x220 and a 1366x300 band, WITH the band's bottom fade composited (90th-percentile luminance, WCAG ratio): guide 1.47 / 2.03 · why 4.15 / 4.17 · FAQ 6.96 / 6.66. Only the FAQ crop clears 4.5:1 at BOTH widths… Moving any h1 ONTO a band needs a fresh measurement of that crop first; do not reuse the figures above for a file that changed." So `if ens_key == 'faq'` is not a page name standing in for a rule; it is the recorded result of the per-page measurement R2 demands, and the procedure for changing it is written down.

2) I re-measured the real deployed renders and the recorded figures hold. From /home/user/ElmsNest/brief/side-pages/pages/verify/*-m-js-full.png I located the band at y=60–282 (222 px ≈ the 220 px of R3; row-mean scan confirms header ends at 60 and the night ground resumes at 284), composited the snippet's own fade (linear-gradient to rgba(2,3,6,.62) over the bottom 36%, elmsnest-s-page-photo/section CSS line 624), and took the 90th-percentile relative luminance of the h1 zone (inset-block-end 20 px, 32 px/1.06 lines) against ink #f4eee3: guide 1.43 (recorded 1.47), FAQ 6.58 measuring the band above the baked-in h1 text (recorded 6.96), why 5.27 mobile but the recorded desktop value 4.17 is what fails the 4.5:1 gate, about 2.63, processing 2.68, contact 1.98, shipping 5.23 mobile. Every non-FAQ crop except shipping is under 4.5:1 on mobile, and the recorded desktop pass/fail is what decides. The measurement matches the code.

3) The evidence's own description confirms the pages already do what it asks. "FAQ gets the on-band h1 … correctly scrimmed … the other six sit off-band because their photographs are too bright" is a verbatim description of R2 (SPEC.md §1 line 19: h1 on the photograph "only where the crop measures ≥ 4.5:1 against the ink (measured, recorded), otherwise directly under it on the night ground"). Being off-band on a bright crop is compliance, not a defect. The home hero the fix invokes as the family model (simplify/verify-after/home-m-js-full.png) is a night photograph — dark ground under the ink — which is why its h1 sits on it; the FAQ's dark asphalt is the only content-page crop in that class. The grammar is "dark enough crop → on-band", and it is applied consistently across both files.

4) The proposed fix re-opens the recorded ruling and would break it. SPEC §2 lists `h1_on` as a snippet parameter ("boolean: the h1 is set on this photograph"), fed by a measured decision; making it an owner-set schema checkbox hands a WCAG 4.5:1 judgement to someone with no way to measure, and would let the guide's 1.43:1 h1 be switched on. That contradicts R2's "measured, recorded" and the §5 budget "the h1 on a band ≥ 4.5:1 (otherwise the h1 moves under the band)". The second half ("once the daylight frames are replaced turn it on for guide, why and about") is speculative about images that do not exist and is already answered by the file's standing instruction to re-measure first. Note also that only the FAQ branch passes `h1_on` at the render site (line 398); the other six branches never pass the parameter at all, so there is no hidden per-page rule to discover.

Residual, non-defect: one could argue `assign ens_h1_on = true` reads more locally inside the `when 'faq'` branch than at line 107. That is cosmetic, not a "should".
vote.scope: In contract (R2 is a recorded §1 ruling, and the finding does not show the ruling's reasoning to be factually wrong — it misses the recorded measurement that backs it). Refuted on the evidence: the measurement exists at elmsnest-s-page.liquid:13–22 and reproduces on the deployed renders.

findings.title: The same h2 and the same CTA pair close two sibling pages
findings.evidence: h2 extraction from the mirrors: processing and shipping both end with עברו 17 ימי עסקים והחבילה לא הגיעה?. page-processing-m-js-full.png y≈1660 and page-shipping-m-js-full.png y≈2110 show the same amber question over the same ליצירת קשר pill and text link — it reads as a template footer, not a page ending.
findings.fix: Keep it on shipping, where the 17-day figure is derived from the table directly above it, and end processing on its own last step instead.

vote.why:
Three of the four factual claims in the evidence are wrong, and the proposed fix's own rationale is wrong.

(1) The named coordinates are not the escalation block. Cropping the real shots: page-processing-m-js-full.png is 390x2216 and page-shipping-m-js-full.png is 390x2688. The crop at processing y=1560-1900 and shipping y=2010-2350 (the y≈1660 / y≈2110 the evidence cites) is the night FOOTER in both — the "קולקציות / מידע" link columns and info@elmsnest.com. The escalation h2 actually sits at y≈1085 on processing and y≈1565 on shipping, ~575 / ~545 px above the cited positions.

(2) "the same amber question" misreads the render. Cropping processing y=1020-1180 and shipping y=1550-2030: the h2 renders in ink white; only the numeral inside <bdi dir="ltr">17</bdi> is amber. It is not an amber heading on either page.

(3) "the same CTA pair" is false — only the pill is shared. theme/sections/elmsnest-s-page.liquid l.501-502 (proc): `env2-btn` ליצירת קשר + `env2-link` **למדיניות המשלוחים המלאה** → ens_ship_pol. l.563-564 (ship): `env2-btn` ליצירת קשר + `env2-link` **מה קורה אחרי שהזמנתם** → ens_proc. Both crops show the two different link texts. The second member differs and each points at what the other page is; shipping's ghost link is the cross-link back to processing. The intros differ too (proc: "…והאימייל ששימש לרכישה — נבדוק את המשלוח מול…"; ship: "…האימייל ששימש לרכישה ותיאור קצר — נבדוק מול…"). What is genuinely shared is the h2 string alone. And the pill+ghost-link close is a family device across the policy pages, not a two-page duplication: help-faq ends the same way (l.462-463, ליצירת קשר + למדיניות המלאה).

(4) The proposed fix's justification inverts the layout. On shipping the section immediately above the escalation is not the times table — it is "ביטול עסקה והחזרות" (14 days / 5% / 100 ₪); the 8–17 figure is two sections up (l.544). On processing the 8–17 figure is the page's own headline plate directly under the h1 (l.483) and the escalation follows the three-step spine that ends at 7–14. So "the 17-day figure is derived from the table directly above it" is true of neither page, and if anything processing owns the number more.

(5) Contract. SPEC.md §0 and §4 keep the copy sentence-for-sentence except the enumerated changes; §4.3 lists what is dropped (the two TOCs, the foot nav, the guide's second button, the duplicate h1) and the escalation block is not among them. COPY-SOURCE.md l.564 records "17 business days → escalate" as a consumer term deliberately present as an h2 on BOTH processing-time and shipping-delivery, and l.525/543 list it in the audit's "worth keeping" for each page. Deleting it from processing would strip the "where is my order" escalation path from the page a waiting customer lands on, for a reason the render contradicts.
vote.scope: In contract but factually refuted: the coordinates point at the footer, the h2 is ink not amber, the CTA pairs differ in their second link (each cross-linking the other page), and the fix's premise about which table sits above the shipping block is wrong; removing the block from processing would also cut copy SPEC §4 keeps verbatim and COPY-SOURCE records as intentionally on both pages.

findings.title: Dek capped at 46ch orphans a word on desktop

findings.fix: Raise to 60ch, or grid ens-page__head like the sections so the lead shares the body column's inline-start edge.

vote.why: The render claim survives inspection, so I cannot refute it — only its numbers and its fix. Pixel scan of /home/user/ElmsNest/brief/side-pages/pages/verify/page-faq-d-js-full.png (1366x1862): the lead's line 1 is y 462-492, x 869->1301 (432px wide) ending "...לא מצאתם תשובה? כתבו"; line 2 is y 496-520, x 1280->1302 (~22px) carrying only the underlined "לנו.". Two of the three cited numbers are wrong: the lead sits at y~470-515, not y~430 (y 400-420 is the credit line "צילום: PumpkinSky"), and the column is 432px, not 330px (46ch x 18px = ~9.4px/ch; elmsnest-s-page.liquid:605 sets 46ch, :729 raises the lead to 18px at >=901). The section body column on the same page measures x 338->937 (~599px ~ 68ch), so no confusion there. It is not out of contract: SPEC §1 records no dek-measure ruling (R9 governs the section grid — 300px heading column + 62-68ch body — and the head is deliberately ungridded), so nothing recorded is being re-opened. Scale is small: desktop only, one page of seven — page-faq-m-js-full.png keeps "כתבו לנו." intact on line 2 (46ch ~ 384px does not bind in a ~342px column), and page-guide-d-js-full.png shows the guide lead breaking into two balanced lines at the same cap. Raising to 60ch or gridding the head changes all seven leads, and desyncs them from home and PDP, to absorb a ~30px overhang on one page. The proportionate fix is to stop the link breaking: a NBSP in "כתבו לנו" or white-space:nowrap on that anchor (elmsnest-s-page.liquid:402), or text-wrap:pretty on .ens-page__lead.
vote.scope: In scope but only as a one-page desktop nit; the observation stands, the stated y/column figures and the 60ch remedy do not.

findings.title: The About link run wraps 3 + 1
findings.evidence: elmsnest-s-page.liquid:688 — .ens-page__run-list is flex-wrap inside the 607px column. In page-about-d-js-full.png (מה תמצאו בחנות, y≈2045) three collection links sit on one line and גרילנדות ותאורה דקורטיבית drops alone underneath.
findings.fix: Give it grid-column:1 / -1, or make it a 2×2 grid.

vote.why: Measured page-about-d-js-full.png (1366x3005, bg RGB 3,6,11). The run is NOT at y~2045 — that row is inside the courtyard photograph; the link run sits at y 2221-2240 (line 1) and y 2261-2280 (line 2). The 3+1 wrap is real: line 1 ink spans x=424..938, line 2 (גרילנדות ותאורה דקורטיבית) x=759..938. Individual link widths are 218 / 81 / 157 / 180 px with 29 px gaps = 720 px of links + 84 px of gaps against a ~607 px 68ch column (inline-start edge x=939) — one line is arithmetically impossible inside the reading measure, so this is not a near-miss. But it is not a defect: (1) SPEC §1 R1 rules the About device to be 'a link run', and a run wraps — the mobile shot page-about-m-js-full.png (y~1790-1830) shows the same device wrapping 2+1+1, so 3+1 on desktop is the family's normal state, not a desktop-only break; a 2x2 grid replaces the ruled run with a different device and, with widths 218 vs 81 px, would give grossly uneven cells. (2) The proposed grid-column:1/-1 breaks R9: elmsnest-s-page.liquid:734 puts every non-h2 child of every section on all seven pages in the 68ch column with the h2 in the 300px margin; only the guide's places frame is deliberately spanned 1/-1 (line 737). Spanning About's run would jut it 364 px past the CTA, signature and every other block and drop it to its own row under the h2. (3) The wrap is not orphaned: both lines are flush to the same inline-start edge (x~938/939) as the gold pill, 'כתבו לנו.' and the signature beneath, reading as one coherent left-ragged block. findings.title: The place cards have ragged bottoms
findings.evidence: page-guide-m-js-full.png y≈880–1120: שביל wraps its title to two lines and קיר does not, so 8 מוצרים ← and 6 מוצרים ← land ~40px apart within the same row and the row bottoms are uneven.
findings.fix: Make .ens-page__place a flex column with justify-content:space-between and a min-block-size so the product count sits on one baseline per row.

vote.why:
Measured page-guide-m-js-full.png (390x3418) pixel by pixel with PIL/numpy over the places frame (y 940-1300).

1. "The row bottoms are uneven" is false. The row bottom is a single continuous 1px rule (colour 37,42,52) at y=1094, spanning x 20-369 with no break (350 px, contiguous) — and the same at y=1274 for the second row. That is exactly what the build produces: .ens-page__places is a `display:grid` (elmsnest-s-page.liquid:648) whose `li` carry `border-block-start` (:649), so grid items stretch to the row height and the two cells in a row end on one shared line. Nothing about the box bottoms is ragged.

2. The stated cause is wrong. Per-column ink bands in row 1 — right/שביל: (948-961 word) (973-985 gloss) (997-1013 title) (1023-1035) (1045-1051) (1067-1075 count); left/קיר: (952-964) (973-985) (1000-1013 title) (1023-1034) (1048-1056 count). Both titles (.ens-page__place-t) occupy a SINGLE line band. What wraps is the licensed sentence .ens-page__place-s («לסימון הדרך, לערוגות ולפינות / הגינה»), which is the licensed pair copy from snippets/elmsnest-s-place (SPEC §4.2) and not editable here.

3. The magnitude is overstated ~2x. The two «מוצרים ←» lines sit 19px apart (1067 vs 1048; second row 1247 vs 1228), which is exactly one 13px/1.45 line box — not "~40px".

4. Desktop, which R9 makes the designed layout, already has all four counts on one baseline (verified in page-guide-d-js-full.png crops at y1400-1620: קיר/גינה/מרפסת counts all at the same y, and שביל's too) because the 4-column grid at ≥901 gives every label one row.

5. The proposed fix is already half-present (`min-block-size:44px` on .ens-page__place, :651) and the other half would trade a 19px inconsistency between the last lines for a 19px hole between each short sentence and its count — the count would detach from the text it belongs to in three of four cells.

So: the evidence misreads the render (titles do not wrap, row bottoms are one shared rule), overstates the offset, and the only real residue is a one-line-height difference in where the last text line falls inside two equal-height mobile cells, caused by fixed licensed copy.
vote.scope: In scope (the guide's places frame, R4) but factually refuted on the render; not a re-opened ruling.

findings.title: Non-interactive squares that read as checkboxes
findings.evidence: elmsnest-s-page.liquid:679 draws a 13×13 hollow square before each __check item (guide §04 at page-guide-m-js-full.png y≈2210, why's שלוש בדיקות). On touch these read as tappable and are not.
findings.fix: Use a short amber rule or a middot instead — the checklist idea without the false affordance.

vote.why:
The geometry in the evidence is right, the inference from it is not, and the fix re-opens a recorded ruling.

What I measured. /home/user/ElmsNest/theme/sections/elmsnest-s-page.liquid:679 is exactly as quoted: `.ens-page__check li::before{content:"";…inline-size:13px;block-size:13px;border:1px solid var(--env2-hair-num)}`. In the real shot /home/user/ElmsNest/brief/side-pages/pages/verify/page-guide-m-js-full.png the first §04 marker occupies x357-369, y2213-2225 — 13x13, one hairline — so the location and size hold. Two `__check` lists exist (lines 234 guide §04, 315 why «שלוש בדיקות»).

Why the affordance claim fails. On these pages the interaction vocabulary is gold plus a 44px target, and the square is in neither family. Sampled from the same guide shot: page ground rgb(5,8,15); the CTA pill below the checklist rgb(255,211,148) (--env2-gold); the square rgb(112,111,110), i.e. --env2-hair-num rgba(244,238,227,.45) — the identical token used for the *structural* hairlines: the spine rail (line 661) and the switch dot. Only one rule in the whole 800-line section sets `cursor:pointer` — line 700, `.ens-page__faq summary` — and that is also the only text control carrying `min-block-size:44px` (the place links at line 651 are the other). The check `li` is 8px padding + 16px/1.45 text ≈ 39px, below the build's own control height, and the marker is a `content:""` pseudo-element on an `li` inside `role="list"`: not focusable, not in the tab order, nothing for a screen reader. Nothing that marks a control on these pages marks this square; a touch user who taps one gets no cursor, no hit target, no colour cue that ever meant "tap" on this page.

Why the fix is worse, and out of scope. SPEC.md §1 R1 records the ruling verbatim — "a hollow-square checklist for the checks" — as part of the atlas device set, carried by named judges (visitor 9, designer 8 «no page reads as one ruled list repeated four times», engineer 9). The finding asks to swap the device for an amber rule or middot; it does not show R1's reasoning (device variety across the seven pages) to be factually wrong, so it re-opens a recorded ruling. And the proposed "short amber rule" would put the marker in the amber/gold family that on these pages *is* the interaction colour (the pill, the FAQ chevron, the hover --env2-glow), while a middot collapses the checklist toward `.ens-page__plain` (line 692) — both push toward the two things R1 ruled against.
vote.scope: Out of contract (SPEC §1 R1 rules the hollow-square checklist device; ruling's reasoning not shown wrong) and the render refutes the premise (marker uses the structural hairline token, no pointer cursor, no 44px target, non-focusable pseudo-element).

findings.title: Hebrew letters wrapped in dir="ltr"
findings.evidence: elmsnest-s-page.liquid:207–209 — <bdi dir="ltr">א</bdi> for the guide §02 markers. The bdi loop exists for Latin/numeric runs; forcing LTR on א/ב/ג is harmless today and wrong the moment a label gains a second character.

vote.why: The quotation is accurate (elmsnest-s-page.liquid:207-209 do wrap א/ב/ג in <bdi dir="ltr">), but every other part of the finding fails. vote.why:

What I measured:

The signature sits at y≈2000-2060, not y≈2450 (y≈2450 is the footer's collection nav; the footer's own contact line «...כתבו לנו: info@elmsnest.com» is at y≈2240). 2. The ruling. /home/user/ElmsNest/brief/side-pages/pages/SPEC.md §1 R6: «About ends signed (letter): «כתבו לנו.» then ElmsNest, ישראל and the store's email address **as text**.» — reason column: Owner 8 («turns the email promise from a policy line into a person»), visitor «the only one I would actually finish reading». findings.title: Desktop inline frames eat a whole fold — the loudest photo in the set is 1243×829
findings.evidence: page-why-d-js-full.png: the solar-cell frame (`ens-page-why-cell.jpg`) spans x 61–1304, y 942–1778 of the 1366×3037 page — 1243×829 px, taller than the 768 px desktop viewport, and it is an electric-cyan high-contrast panel close-up on the darkest ground in the store. page-about-d-js-full.png repeats it: the bench frame runs x 61–1304 at the same 3:2 (y ≈2270–2380 crop shown, full frame 1240×827). Cause is CSS in /home/user/ElmsNest/theme/sections/elmsnest-s-page.liquid: `.ens-page__fig--inline img{aspect-ratio:3 / 2}` with `.ens-page__brk` being a bare `.env2-wrap` (max 1240 px) and no desktop cap — the @media (min-width:901px) block only re-caps the BAND (`block-size:300px`), never the inline frame. R3 caps the band at 300 px precisely so no photograph owns a fold; the inline frame escapes that discipline and owns one.
findings.fix: In the @media (min-width:901px) block of elmsnest-s-page.liquid add a cap for the inline frame: `.ens-page__fig--inline img{max-block-size:440px;aspect-ratio:auto;block-size:440px}` (keep `object-fit:cover` and `object-position:var(--ens-op-lg,…)`), or constrain the wrapper instead — `.ens-page__brk{max-inline-size:860px}` — so the why-cell and about-court frames land at roughly half a fold, the same proportion the 300 px band holds.

vote.why:
I measured the two shots the finding names, the ten assets, and the CSS. The geometry is roughly right; the two claims that make it a "should" are wrong.

1) It does NOT eat a fold. Measured on page-why-d-js-full.png (1366×3037) by row/column variance: the inline frame occupies y 952–1778, x 63–1302 = **1240×826** (the finding said 1243×829 — close). page-about-d-js-full.png: the same frame at y **1286–2113** = 1240×827 (the finding's "y ≈2270–2380" is simply not where it is; only its 1240×827 number is right). The desktop fold in THIS round is not 768: brief/side-pages/simplify/verify.js:20 and verify-mirror.js:44 both declare `VIEWS = [['m',390,844],['s',360,640],['d',1366,900]]`, and page-why-d-js-fold.png / page-about-d-js-fold.png are literally 1366×**900**. 826 < 900. The frame is 92% of a viewport, not "taller than the viewport", and it sits mid-page (y 952 of 3037 on why — after the band, h1, lead, §01 heading and prose), so it never competes with the fold at all.

2) It is NOT "the loudest photo in the set" — it is the flattest. Per-asset luminance over all ten theme/assets/ens-page-*.jpg: ens-page-why-cell.jpg (1200×800, exactly 3:2, so object-fit:cover shows the whole file) is L=111, **Lstd=44 — the LOWEST contrast of the ten** (range 44–66), p95L=200. ens-page-contact-band.jpg is brighter and far louder (L=113, Lstd=66, p95=232); ens-page-about-court.jpg p95=216; ens-page-why-band.jpg is more saturated (0.69 vs 0.57). Confirmed on the rendered pixels: why inline region L=111/std=42/p95=199 vs the contact page's *band* at L=107/std=69/p95=232. The "electric-cyan high-contrast panel on the darkest ground" reading is a misread of a deep-navy cell close-up that is the most tonally consonant frame in the set with the night ground.

3) It re-opens a recorded ruling on reasoning that isn't in it. SPEC §1 R3 reads "**The band** is short. ≤ 220 px at 390 and ≤ 300 px at ≥ 901, **so the page's first decision is at the fold**" — it is scoped to the opening band and justified by the first decision, not by "no photograph owns a fold" as the finding restates it. The build honours it exactly (page-why band measured y 70–370 = 300px; CSS line 730 `.ens-page__fig--band img{block-size:300px}`). R7 goes the other way: the loud pictures "are inline and cropped" — inline is the *sanctioned* home for a loud frame, and the four R7 names (Haifa terraces, cactus park, Kew borders, bougainvillea wall) do not include the solar cell, which is the set's only «מנגנון» per §3. R9 asks desktop to be a designed layout, and a full-wrap 3:2 plate with the caption in the 300px margin column (`.ens-page__figcap-in`) is that design. §5's budgets are all met and desktop is proportionally shorter as required (why 3.37 d vs 3.57 m; about 3.34 vs 3.52; all seven under cap).

4) The proposed fix fights the code's recorded reason. The comment at elmsnest-s-page.liquid:612–613 says `block-size:auto` is required or the `height` attribute (a presentational hint) beats `aspect-ratio` and the frame grows; the fix's `block-size:440px` re-introduces exactly that fragility, and at 1240 wide it crops the 3:2 to ~2.8:1 — i.e. it turns the one inline frame back into a band, which is the shape R7 forbids for a loud picture. The `.ens-page__brk{max-inline-size:860px}` alternative would desync the frame from the 300px+68ch caption grid.

One real (unclaimed) nit I did find while measuring: ens-page-why-cell.jpg is 1200×800 native but renders into 1240 CSS px, a ~3% upscale. That is not the finding.
vote.scope: theme/sections/elmsnest-s-page.liquid (.ens-page__fig--inline, @media min-width:901px) as rendered in brief/side-pages/pages/verify/page-why-d-js-full.png and page-about-d-js-full.png; measured against SPEC.md §1 R3/R7/R9, §3, §5 and the round's 1366×900 desktop viewport.

findings.title: The FAQ's accordion chevron points left/right, never down — the logical-property rule is broken for the one glyph that is directional
findings.evidence: page-faq-m-js-fold.png: at x≈30, the OPEN first row («האם כל המוצרים בחנות סולאריים?», y≈500) shows a chevron pointing RIGHT «›», and the three CLOSED rows (y≈627, 677, 730) show chevrons pointing LEFT «‹». Neither state points down or up, so open and closed read as «back» and «forward», not as expand/collapse; on the open row a right-pointing chevron reads as a link arrow. Cause, elmsnest-s-page.liquid: `.ens-page__faq summary::after{border-block-end:1px solid var(--env2-gold);border-inline-end:1px solid var(--env2-gold);transform:rotate(45deg)}` mixes a physical side (block-end) with a logical one (inline-end). The section hardcodes `dir="rtl"`, so inline-end resolves to LEFT, the corner bisector starts at down-left instead of down-right, and every rotation lands 90° off the intended down/up pair.
findings.fix: The glyph is geometry, not layout, so give it physical sides: change `border-block-end`/`border-inline-end` to `border-bottom:1px solid var(--env2-gold);border-right:1px solid var(--env2-gold)`. Leave `inset-inline-end:6px` (the positioning is correctly logical) and leave `rotate(45deg)` closed / `rotate(-135deg)` open — with physical borders those now render down when closed and up when open in both directions.

vote.why: Could not refute; the finding is confirmed by both code and pixels. (1) elmsnest-s-page.liquid:702-703 is exactly as quoted (border-block-end + border-inline-end, rotate(45deg) closed / rotate(-135deg) open) and line 153 hardcodes dir="rtl" on the section root, so inline-end resolves to LEFT: bordered corner is bottom-left, vector (-1,+1) = 135deg (y-down, clockwise); +45deg -> 180deg = LEFT closed, -135deg -> 0deg = RIGHT open. (2) Cropped page-faq-m-js-fold.png at (0,470)-(80,760) and read it: the open first row (<details open>, line 408) shows a right-pointing ">" at x~30, y~495; the three closed rows below show left-pointing "<". No down/up state renders — the evidence's read of the shot is accurate. (3) Decisive corroboration: the identical device is already written correctly twice elsewhere in this theme, with comments naming this exact failure — elmsnest-s-pdp-facts.liquid:239-241 ("The old -45deg / 135deg pair pointed RIGHT / LEFT, i.e. back / forward in RTL") and elmsnest-s-coll-header.liquid:149-153 ("border-inline-end gave bottom-left (-1,+1) -> LEFT, the shape of a back link"). The page section regressed a documented house fix, so this is a family-consistency defect, not a taste call. One correction to the proposed fix: physical border-bottom/border-right would render correctly but breaks SPEC.md §2 line 45 ("logical properties") and diverges from both precedents; the in-family fix is border-inline-start + border-block-end (bottom-right corner in RTL), leaving rotate(45deg)/rotate(-135deg) and inset-inline-end:6px untouched.
vote.scope: In scope. SPEC.md §1 records no ruling on the FAQ chevron or its geometry, so nothing is re-opened; §2 line 45 ("logical properties") governs only how the fix should be written, not whether the glyph should point down/up. Single-line CSS change in theme/sections/elmsnest-s-page.liquid:702.

vote.why:
Both headline allegations are factually wrong, and the residue is a stale planning table, not a defect in what shipped.

What I measured:
1. The render is correct and honest. verify.json (`brief/side-pages/pages/verify/verify.json`, all seven `*-m-js` entries) reports ten photographs with `captionFound`, `kickerFound` and `creditFound` all true and `photosMissing: []` on every page. About: band «מקום · חצר בירושלים, בצל» / inline «מקום · ספסל בגינה». I cropped `page-about-m-js-full.png` (390×2973) at 0–560 and 1720–2260 and read both crops: the band is the Jerusalem courtyard with the millstone under «צילום: RonAlmog (CC BY 2.0)»; the inline frame carries «צילום: Basile Morin (CC BY-SA 4.0)». Row for row, IMAGES.md and the render agree — including all four captions the finding calls "rewritten".

2. «Never authorised» is contradicted by the finding's own evidence. `wm_faf95922bd` is CC BY-SA 4.0, is in IMAGES.md (which the task itself names as the round's photograph-and-licence record), is credited on the render, and I opened `theme/assets/ens-page-about-court.jpg` (1000×667): a garden bench, no fixture that could read as a store product, captioned «ספסל בגינה» — no location claim made. The finding's own PROPOSED FIX concedes «the licences in IMAGES.md are correct and the assets are already correctly credited on the render», which is the opposite of unauthorised.

3. «Dropped in silence» is false in three places. Commit `bc1d9bd` («content pages: five band photographs re-cropped or replaced») states the reason in its body: «the About band no longer uses the Garden of the Righteous at Yad Vashem — a memorial is not decorative brand imagery — and shows the Sergei Courtyard instead, with a garden bench at golden hour inline.» The same commit rewrote the IMAGES.md rows (I read the diff: `wm_d5e6fd1fe6` out, `wm_faf95922bd` in). And `elmsnest-s-page.liquid` lines ~19–23 record «The five photographs replaced or re-cropped on 2026-09-08 (about band, about court, contact, processing, shipping)» — a comment the finding itself quotes while calling the change silent. Three written records with a stated reason is not silence.

4. The four caption changes are honesty corrections, not drift. Each drops a claim its source does not support: why-band «זריחה» → «אור נמוך» (source is Dülmen Wildpark, no documented sunrise); processing «אחר הצהריים» → «בקיו» (Kew Gardens Mediterranean Garden — the place is verifiable, the hour is not); contact «חצר בחיפה» → «גן בחיפה» (the source file is Baha'i **Garden**, Haifa); guide drops «מעל גינה» from a sky crop. Nothing deployed is wrong: no licence, no credit, no caption, ≤3 photographs per page, 10 frames, About at 3.52 screens against a 4.5 budget. The finding asks for a documentation tidy of a superseded planning table while explicitly forbidding any theme change — that is not «should» severity on the deployed content pages.

The one point in its favour: the pdp round did amend its spec (`55d9326`), so a house habit exists, and a stale §3 table is a real minor inconsistency worth a note. That is a nice-to-have, not the «unauthorised frame / silent drop» defect the finding reports.
vote.scope: In-round (SPEC §3 photograph table / IMAGES.md bookkeeping) but not a defect in the deployed pages; the substantive change it questions — removing the Yad Vashem Garden of the Righteous — is a recorded honesty/decency decision the finding does not challenge.

vote.why: Measured, not assumed. verify.json (page-about-m-js.pageCopy.photos) confirms the deployed caption is «מקום · ספסל בגינה» with credit found — so the string is real, but the argument around it fails on four measured points. (1) Geometry: cropping page-about-m-js-full.png (390x2973), the inline frame spans y≈1447–1682, not the claimed 1730–2130; the caption/credit pair sits at y≈1700–1720 and «ElmsNest, ישראל» at y≈2023 — ~320px apart with a whole «מה תמצאו בחנות» section (h2, four collection links, the gold pill, the guide link) between. It is not "directly above" the signature. (2) Honesty: the frame is unmistakably tropical (fan palms, banana-family foliage, blue sky) and cannot be misread as an Israeli courtyard, and «צילום: Basile Morin (CC BY-SA 4.0)» prints on its own line immediately under the caption — the build's own signal that this is a licensed third-party photograph. No fabricated claim exists. (3) The inconsistency premise is factually wrong. All ten cap_* defaults in theme/sections/elmsnest-s-page.liquid (lines 767–850): six name no place at all — שמיים בין ערביים, חצר אחת בשעת בין ערביים, אור נמוך בין עצים (Dülmen, Germany), תא סולארי מקרוב, שביל בגינה (NBG, USA), מטע זיתים. Only three name one (ירושלים, קיו, חיפה). Not naming the place is the majority grammar, and two other foreign frames go unnamed, so the build does not "name the foreign place when it is inconvenient". (4) The fix does not fix the stated defect: the title complains the place is unlabelled, yet «ספסל בגן בוטני, שעת זהב» still never names Singapore — it swaps one unlabelled place for another, while asserting an hour the rendered crop does not obviously show (bright blue sky, flat mid-frame light), which is a weaker §3 position than saying nothing. Half the fix targets «תמונת החצר», a theme-editor schema label (line 809) that no customer ever sees, so BRIEF §3 does not reach it. And the requested SPEC §3 mirror has no target: SPEC §3's About rows are wm_d5e6fd1fe6 «חורשה בירושלים…» (band) and ov_f33051a3 «חצר בירושלים, בצל» (inline), while the build ships ov_f33051a3 as the band and wm_faf95922bd (Basile Morin) as the inline — there is no row for this photograph. SPEC §6 owner item 2 further records this exact tension already ("every Israeli frame in the pool is midday; the golden-hour places are Mediterranean-looking but photographed elsewhere"), disposing of it as an owner photograph swap. Residual kernel: R5 and the snippet header (snippets/elmsnest-s-page-photo.liquid: "caption  the subject and the hour") do want an hour, and «ספסל בגינה» carries none — but that gap is shared with cap_proc_band «גינה ים-תיכונית בקיו», so it is not the single-page honesty failure claimed and is at most a one-word tidy, not a "should".
vote.scope: In-round on R5 compliance (a compliance claim, not a re-opening of a §1 ruling), and the small R5 "and the hour" gap is genuine and shared with the processing caption. But the finding as written is refuted: its geometry is mis-measured, its honesty argument is unsupported by the render, its "inconsistent" premise is contradicted by six of ten captions, its fix does not deliver its own headline, half of it edits non-rendered theme-editor schema labels, and its SPEC §3 target row does not describe this photograph. The golden-hour framing additionally presses against SPEC §6 owner item 2, which already records this disposition.
