The geometry is right; the load-bearing premise is empirically false, so the fix cannot be taken and the shortfall is not a defect.

WHAT I CONFIRMED. The five file sizes are as stated (PIL on theme/assets: about-court 1000x667 181 KiB, why-band 1200x802 181, why-cell 1200x800 192, faq-band 1200x1176 189, about-band 1200x751 194; the other five are 1600 wide). `.ens-page__brk` is a bare `env2-wrap` with only `margin-block-start` (section CSS lines 632/735), and `.env2-wrap{width:min(var(--env2-w),100% - 2*var(--env2-gut))}` with `--env2-w:1240px; --env2-gut:clamp(20px,4vw,64px)` (elmsnest-v2-core.liquid:21,118) → 1240 px at 1366. WHAT REFUTES IT. "Weight is not the constraint" is the claim the whole finding rests on, and it is wrong for exactly these five files. I re-ran the round's own pipeline (pdp3/images/prepare-assets.py: LANCZOS resize, progressive JPEG, quality stepped down from 82 with a q55 floor) on the same sources IMAGES.md names, at 1600 px:
  about-court 392 KiB @q54 · why-band 272 · why-cell 262 · faq-band 261 · about-band 245
Every one blows the 210 KB per-asset cap after the ladder has hit its floor. about-court cannot even hold the cap at 1200 px (214 KiB @q54) — which is precisely why it shipped at 1000. The 1600 px files cited as proof that "the budget holds at that width" are a different class of picture: guide-band is 0.076 B/px (sky), shipping 1600x535 and processing 1600x483 are short crops. The five short files are 0.19-0.28 B/px — dense foliage and a solar-cell macro. Averaging the two classes is the error.

The proposed "drop quality as needed" lands at q40 (why-band), q42 (faq-band) and q22 (about-court) to reach 210 KB at 1600. Trading a 1.24x resample of a q70 file for a q22 file is a plain net loss in the one image the finding cares most about.

The per-page budget kills it independently: SPEC §5 caps a page at 420 KB of images. about is 375 KiB today and would be 637 KiB with both files at 1600 (why: 373 -> 534). The fix breaks a second recorded budget.

The render shows no defect: the about-court frame and the why band at 1366 (page-why-d-js-full.png y0-340) are both clean; a 1.14-1.24x resample of a photograph is invisible at DPR 1. The DPR-2 line is not specific to these five — no file in the set, 1600 px included, can serve a 1366 px band at DPR 2 (that wants 2732 px); that is a recorded budget choice, not a per-file bug. "Every desktop" also overstates: the wrap only reaches 1000 px above a ~1087 px viewport.

Contract: SPEC §3 specifies "≤ 1600 px, ≤ 210 KB ... srcset candidates ≤ the file" — a ceiling, not a floor. The build meets all of it, and the finding concedes the snippet's candidate logic is correct. The only remaining option it offers, capping `.ens-page__brk` to 1000 px for about, would break R9's desktop layout (the inline frame is the full reading wrap on every other page) to cure an invisible 1.24x.

The CSS observation is half-true, but the evidence's geometry is wrong, the framing overstates it, and the proposed fix cannot work as written.

The claim's «trio real y≈1394–1729» is off by ~228 px — that band is item 3 + the note + the next h2 («עברו 17 ימי עסקים»). Its height (335 px) matches, so this was measured on some other render, not the shot it cites. No page has a trio there: about's trio rules are 1095/1203/1311, and guide has no trio at all (grep: pair at 216 guide + 527 ship; trio at 355 about + 551 ship).

2) "Back to back" is false. Measured gap between the pair's closing rule (643) and the trio's first rule (1166) is 523 px — an entire section between them (the spine, three items, plus a 3-line note), under its own h2. At 390x844 that is ~62% of a viewport; they are not consecutive lists, and the finding's own text concedes the spine sits between.

3) They are not "the same recipe" even at ≤900. Measured in the shot and in the CSS (lines 669–685): the pair is a closed list — `:last-child{border-block-end}` produces the third rule at y=643 that shuts it; the trio is an open run of top-ruled blocks with no closing rule after item 3 (none detected after 1406). Title 17px vs 18px, block padding 14/14 vs 14/18, `dd` is a one/two-line answer vs `trio p` a paragraph with `margin-block-start:6px; max-inline-size:52ch`. Beyond that, the `--ens-page-line` top hairline is the page family's rule, not a device signature: it is shared by 6 of the 9 devices (places frame, pair, trio, plain list, faq `details`, plate cells).
